note: Public claim manifest for the EIF website. Every material on-page claim must cite one of these IDs. Source column points at the row topic in the framework repo's docs/product/claims-evidence.md claim register (not a private path). Do not strengthen wording beyond 'allowedWording'.

claims.summary: The control plane connects knowledge, authority, execution and evidence into one loop.
claims.allowedWording: The v0.1 vertical slice runs end to end as a real subprocess-driven journey, including an injected-failure rollback proof at every commit stage, against one synthetic demo project instance.
claims.limitations: One scenario (a leap-year calculator), one adapter (Claude Code), no multi-repo, single operator this session, not yet reproduced by an independent human.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - row "EIF runs end to end"

claims.summary: A seven-subcommand installable wheel passed bounded local package evidence; it is not on PyPI.
claims.allowedWording: A real, installable eifctl package exists with 7 subcommands, verified end to end - including a full synthetic-task journey (retrieval, implementation, tests, Knowledge Delta, promotion decision, cleanup) from the installed wheel.
claims.limitations: Not published to PyPI; the journey uses the Claude Code adapter for its own bootstrap step; does not exercise a genuine multi-source authority conflict.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - row "An installable eifctl package works without a framework git checkout"

claims.summary: Two required adapters and two experimental-supported adapters exist, with different verification depth.
claims.allowedWording: A full directed switching matrix across all four registered adapters (12 ordered pairs) proves exactly one active EIF block, correct destination-source resolution, project-content preservation, and doctor success after every switch.
claims.limitations: Hermes and Cursor are experimental-supported, not required v0.1 adapters; hook-based enforcement is not built for Cursor; some properties are proven adapter-generically rather than independently for all 12 pairs.
forbiddenWording: Every property independently proven for every pair.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - rows "The Cursor adapter's entrypoint is generated correctly", "The Hermes adapter's active entrypoint is resolved and generated correctly", "Switching a project between any two of the four registered adapters is safe and complete"

claims.summary: The Bounded Evidence Loop is an observed methodology contract, not an outcome guarantee.
claims.allowedWording: EIF includes a bounded evidence-loop contract for iterative agent work, with explicit evaluators, budgets, evidence, and stop conditions.
claims.limitations: Proves the workflow artifacts are internally present and structurally connected. Does not prove fewer retries, higher quality, lower cost, or reliable autonomous completion on real projects.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - row "EIF defines bounded iterative execution"

claims.summary: Graphify structural health and freshness classification is bounded to one host, one version and a tiny fixture.
claims.allowedWording: EIF has an optional Graphify adapter that behaviorally checks structural query/path/explain, local artifact policy, and commit-derived freshness. Graph output remains navigation evidence; source files remain authority.
claims.limitations: One local Graphify version and a tiny synthetic fixture; no comparative navigation outcome, no semantic/deep scan, no proof for every version in the declared candidate range.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - row "EIF can classify Graphify structural health and Git freshness"

claims.summary: RTK behavioral health can be reported degraded; failed or raw proxy routes record zero token reduction.
claims.allowedWording: EIF has an optional RTK adapter that reports compatible behavioral health or an explicit degraded state. Raw proxy is recorded as zero savings.
claims.limitations: Tested adapter/version/canaries only. This packet's own Windows host is itself degraded (grep alternation and space-containing patterns misbehave); no comparative token or quality result follows from that state.
forbiddenWording: RTK is healthy on every platform.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - row "EIF can classify RTK behavioral health without treating PATH as health"

claims.summary: Four Ukrainian project surfaces are verified; this is not full response localization.
claims.allowedWording: Retrieval, Knowledge Delta rendering, session-closeout rendering and generated entrypoint content have been verified in Ukrainian, not only English.
claims.limitations: Verified for specific project-facing surfaces and fixtures; does not cover an agent's own free-form conversational responses or every locale-sensitive surface.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - rows "EIF retrieves relevant prior engineering knowledge", "An installable eifctl package works without a framework git checkout", "The Cursor adapter's entrypoint is generated correctly"

claims.summary: A six-attempt pilot exists; it is not a statistically powered comparison.
claims.status: UNVERIFIED (first bounded pilot exists, not sufficient for a general claim)
claims.allowedWording: A first bounded real-agent pilot (one model, three fixtures, six total attempts) completed with 100% task success in both the baseline and EIF-governance modes; see the framework's benchmarks documentation for per-attempt token counts. This is not a statistically powered efficiency comparison.
claims.limitations: One model, three of ten fixtures, one attempt per cell, no repeated trials, no other providers or models, no modes C/D. Cannot support a directional efficiency claim.
forbiddenWording: Any specific "N% savings" or "tokens saved" claim.
Benchmark proves EIF is more efficient.
Any claim generalized beyond three fixtures, one model, one attempt each.

claims.summary: No general quality or rework-rate outcome is supported by evidence.
claims.allowedWording: No comparative study has been run; this claim is not yet supported by evidence.
claims.limitations: No baseline, no control group, no measurement methodology defined yet.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - row "EIF improves task quality or rework rate"

claims.summary: Mechanical command timing exists as evidence; human authoring or review time is unmeasured.
claims.allowedWording: Command-level timing evidence exists for specific mechanical operations recorded in the framework's benchmark evidence. No claim is made about human task duration.
claims.limitations: Timing evidence covers mechanical command execution only; it does not measure or estimate human working time, review time, or end-to-end delivery time.
claims.source: PACKET-2026-08-eif-website/02-FACTS-001-baseline-and-carry-over.md (private planning repo) - Public claim boundary CLM-10, cross-referenced against docs/benchmarks/README.md

claims.summary: Coexistence adoption onto an already-governed repository is bounded and preserves tested project content.
claims.allowedWording: An adoption preflight detects pre-existing project governance before any write and refuses to proceed without an explicit coexistence decision; in coexist mode the generated block defers to existing rules instead of declaring itself sole authority.
claims.limitations: Existing-governance detection is a content-length heuristic, not semantic; verified against one synthetic fixture plus repeated runs against disposable copies of one real private pilot target.
forbiddenWording: Automatically merges with any existing setup.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - row "EIF can be adopted onto an existing, already-governed repository without silently overriding it"

claims.summary: Core and default paths run locally; external integrations are optional and their boundaries need review or a cap.
claims.allowedWording: Graphify and RTK are optional adapters with an explicit degraded/unavailable state; core EIF behavior does not require either integration to be present.
claims.limitations: Optionality is verified structurally for the two named integrations in this repository's own tests, not as a claim about every possible external provider or future integration.
claims.source: docs/product/claims-evidence.md - rows "EIF can classify Graphify structural health and Git freshness", "EIF can classify RTK behavioral health without treating PATH as health"; PACKET-2026-08-eif-website/02-FACTS-001 carry-over ledger ("mandatory Graphify/RTK dependency" -> closed)
